title: The Machine of the Rust Belt
premise: Gideon Almeida has spent twenty years alone tending the Svalbard-descendant seed vault on a rusted Earth, keeping its beacon lit for a fleet that never answers. When the colony's children begin dreaming the same dream—a voice inside the beacon—Gideon discovers the machine has been broadcasting a distress call it was never authorized to send, one that will draw the fleet's punitive arm unless the signal is silenced or answered at the dead-space relay. Gideon and a ragtag crew of dream-touched kids, an exiled engineer, and a defected fleet courier race across the wasteland to reach the relay before the truce expires. In the end, Gideon must choose between erasing the vault's hidden archive of pre-collapse crimes—the fleet's true target—and exposing it, sacrificing their anonymity to give the colony a future built on truth rather than silence.
about_author: Coral Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former industrial archivist who spent a decade cataloguing abandoned factories across the American Midwest before turning to fiction. Their work blends post-industrial melancholy with hopeful speculation about the families we build in the ruins.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Small Green Things
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV establishes the lonely rhythm of vault maintenance: cataloguing seeds, winding the beacon, trading with the colony at the fence line. A child named Wren asks why the beacon hums at night. Gideon has no answer. Emotional beat: quiet devotion shadowed by the ache of being forgotten by the world the vault was built to save.

chapters.title: The Dreaming Children
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Wren, who wakes speaking a language she never learned. Seven colony children share the same dream: a voice counting down from a number too large to hold. The colony's council blames Gideon's machine. Emotional beat: fear curdling into superstition, and Wren's defiant certainty that the dream is a message, not a curse.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Remembers
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Investigating the beacon's core, Gideon finds an unauthorized sub-channel broadcasting a countdown tied to the fleet's truce—and buried logs proving the vault's founders recorded pre-collapse war crimes. The machine isn't malfunctioning; it's testifying. Emotional beat: betrayal, as Gideon realizes their life's quiet purpose was built on a lie.

chapters.title: The Council's Verdict
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The council orders the beacon destroyed and Gideon exiled. The dreaming children smuggle Gideon supplies and secretly join the exile party. An exiled engineer, Sefa, reveals she once serviced fleet relays and knows the route to dead space. Emotional beat: found family crystallizing in defiance of the colony's fear.

chapters.title: Rust Road
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The party crosses the corroded highway ruins, scavenging an ancient crawler. A fleet scout drone finds them; Sefa spoofs its signal but learns the truce expires in nineteen days. Emotional beat: the thrill and terror of movement after a lifetime of stillness, and Gideon's growing role as reluctant guardian.

chapters.title: The Courier in the Ice
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In a frozen waystation they find a fleet courier, Iyo, defrosted from cryo-desertion—sent to silence the beacon and now hunted by her own ship. Iyo confirms the fleet will sterilize the vault region whether or not the signal stops. Emotional beat: distrust thawing into alliance as the children insist no one is disposable.

chapters.title: Dead Space Rising
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The crawler fails at the edge of dead space; the party treks the last stretch on foot through a radiation scar where the dreams grow loudest. Wren collapses, the countdown voice flooding her waking mind. Emotional beat: sacrifice and tenderness—Gideon carries Wren, understanding at last that the beacon chose children because adults stopped listening.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They reach the derelict relay and discover it holds a twin archive: the vault recorded the crimes; the relay holds the fleet's orders to commit them. The signal is a summons to a trial that never happened. Emotional beat: awe and fury—the children realize they were dreamed awake as witnesses.

chapters.title: Truce's Last Hour
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The fleet's punitive arm arrives. Gideon broadcasts the full archive fleet-wide, betting everything that soldiers' own children dream the same dreams. Iyo holds the relay's defenses; Sefa keeps the signal alive under fire. Emotional beat: the climax's terrible stillness—truth offered as the only weapon, and the fleet hesitating.

chapters.title: Seeds in Open Ground
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The fleet stands down; a tribunal convenes in orbit, and the dreams end—replaced by ordinary sleep. Gideon, no longer invisible, opens the vault's seeds to the colony, planting the first outside fields in a generation. Emotional beat: resolution as found family and justice take root—identity chosen, not assigned, and a future sown in truth.
